5.2   BYLAW NO. 2099

      "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 693, (971 Walfred Road) Bylaw No. 2099,
      2023".

      The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2099 at 7:52 p.m.

      Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Pat Guiney has applied on behalf of
      1157393 BC Ltd. to amend the zoning of 971 Walfred Road from the One- and Two-
      Family Zone to the Residential Townhouse 1 Zone.


      This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of approximately 13
      townhouses.


      Prior to Public Hearing, the applicant has provided a technical memo from an engineer
      that verifies stormwater can be adequately managed on-site for the proposed
      development, which has been approved by the Director of Engineering AND a memo by
      a Landscape Architect that examines existing trees on site and along the frontages to
      provide comment on potential tree retention, which has been approved by the Director
      of Planning.

In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:
1. Amenity Contributions as a bonus for increased density as follows:
a. $610 per unit towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; and
b. $3,660 per unit towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund.


2. Road dedication, full frontage improvements, a stormwater management plan, and a
construction parking plan — all to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;


3. Onsite paver stones, an arbour with a pedestrian gate, and variable rooflines — all to
the satisfaction of the Director of Planning;


4. That storage within garages does not prevent parking of vehicles, tree protection
measures are carried out throughout the entire construction period, and that concrete
used will comply with Council's Low Carbon Concrete Policy;


5. With respect to the neighbouring property at 3303 Lodmell, the developer will install
drainage improvements, remove the existing retaining wall, install a 6-foot fence along
the shared property line, retain trees along the shared property line, and plant an
additional 8 tree along the shared property line.


This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan 'Neighbourhood'
designation.


Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local Government
Act.

Mayor Goodmanson called a first time for presentations.

Pat Guinev, Applicant - expressed support for the proposed development and provided
an overview of some energy efficient features of the build including solar energy, electric
car chargers, heat pumps, electric water heaters and induction cook tops. Speaker also
concerned about parking in the area, noting visitor spots including oversized parking
that will be accessible.

Mayor Goodmanson called a second time for presentations.

D. Knudson, Lodmell Rd - expressed concerns with the proposed development including
changes to the neighbourhood over time, effects of previous developments have had on
the speaker's property, and proposed possible remedies for Council's consideration.

L. Plomp, Whimfield Terr - expressed support for the proposed development including
extensive public engagement undertaken by the applicant, and addressing of close
proximity resident's concerns.

Mendez, Mesa PI - expressed concern with the proposed development including concern
for safety of children and pedestrians in the area, size of the proposed buildings, and
emergency safety considerations.

M. Wignall, Selwyn Rd - expressed support for the proposed development including the
applicants work in the community previously.

J.Patterson, Lodmell Rd - expressed concerns with parking within and nearby the
proposed development and concern for safety of children and pedestrians in the area.

Mayor Goodmanson called a third time for presenters.

Councillor Wagner inquired to the Engineering Department. What is the current parking
situation near the proposed development?

K.Balzer, Director of Engineering and Public Works responded - there is currently no
visitor parking on Lodmell Rd, only on Walfred Rd. Parking issues, should they arise, will
be monitored by the Bylaw Enforcement Department. No parking or limited parking
signage would be erected if necessary.

Councillor Wagner inquired to the Engineering Department. Is the current parking there
scalloped?

K. Balzer, Director of Engineering and Public Works responded confirming the scalloped
parking style on Walfred Rd.

Councillor Szpak inquired to staff and Council. Regarding the neighbour at 3303 Lodmell
Rd who has been experiencing difficulties, what can be done to mitigate these issues?

M. Baldwin, Director of Planning responded - staff included the owners of 3303 Lodmell
Rd's concerns as conditions of zoning.

Councillor Szpak wished to confirm that the conditions of zoning as presented were
amenable to the owner of 3303 Lodmell Rd.

D. Knudson, Lodmell Rd - responded confirming these conditions are satisfactory.

Councillor Harder inquired to the Engineering Department. Based off the traffic safety
comments, it appears that the landscaping plans show a sheltered area with pavers and
a bench for those waiting for the bus. Preferably, this is landscaped like the rest of
Walfred Rd.

K. Balzer, Director of Engineering and Public Works responded confirming the bench and
shelter will be present with a 2.2m sidewalk that connects to the existing ones on
Walfred Rd as well as a stop sign on Lodmell Rd.

Councillor Harder noted appreciation for comments regarding families reducing to one
vehicle.

Mayor Goodmanson inquired to the Engineering and Public Works Department. Is the
parking on Walfred signed for use by this development or is it for anyone?

K. Balzer, Director of Engineering and Public Works responded confirming the parking
spots are for the public.

             Mayor Goodmanson declared the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2099 closed at 8:18 pm.

6.   PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

     Councillor Harder left the meeting at 8:18 p.m.

     Mayor Goodmanson opened the public participation period.

     Councillor Harder returned to the meeting at 8:19 p.m.

     S. Perry, Glen Lake Rd — re: item 4.1— Speaker expressed opposition to the City joining the CRD
     Arts and Culture Program noting Langford and Victoria do not share a border. Speaker also
     encouraged the City to plan for an arts and culture space within the new university building.
     Speaker expressed a wish for Langford's money to stay within the municipality. Speaker
     expressed concern for safety within the City of Victoria and cautioned Council against providing
     funding. re: item 4.2 —Speaker expressed concern with electric water heating tanks noting costs
     associated with this feature including insurance and replacement. Speaker also noted electric
     water heating tanks occupy a large amount of space.

     J. Withers, Woodhampton Rise — re: item 4.1 — Speaker expressed support for the City joining
     the CRD Arts and Culture Program noting a need to travel into Victoria currently to experience
     live music and a wish to have this form of entertainment locally. Speaker noted that music
     fosters a sense of community and local identity.

     J. Rye, Finney Rd — re: item 13.1 — Speaker attempted to address an item that was the subject of
     a previous Public Hearing. As a result, the speaker was interrupted and their comments
     disallowed.

     S. Sifert, Walfred Rd — re: 9.1.7 Speaker expressed concern with the report noting that
     homelessness and camping in public spaces cause negative impacts to residents and businesses.
     Speaker noted that shelters are appearing in many places throughout the City and consideration
     of residents and business safety is important.

     R. Louie, Bellamy Rd — re: item 4.1 —Speaker expressed opposition to the City joining the
     program as there is no opt out feature. Speaker also noted that Langford organizations are not
     guaranteed to receive funding from the program and if they do, it may not be proportionate.
     Speaker noted that the funding should stay within the community and the funding rates through
     the CRD may increase in the future.

     M. Morton, Phelps Ave — re: item 13.5 —Speaker expressed concern with the Tree Bylaw noting
     that homeowners and residents of Langford are experiencing issues with the Bylaw including
     adverse financial effects and unfair process.

     M. Wignall, 2375 Selwyn Rd — re: item 4.1 —Speaker expressed concern with the costs of the
     CRD Arts and Culture program noting the City may not receive the value for the money invested.
     re: item 13.7 —Speaker expressed concern with sheltering within the City, noting the difficult
     relationship between enforcement and allowing sheltering to occur from a public safety
     perspective.

     W. Bowers, Millstream Rd — re: item 4.1 — Speaker expressed concern with the CRD Arts and
     Culture program noting high costs. Speaker also noted that outreach to directly neighbouring
     municipalities is needed and could result in more programs locally rather than providing money
     to the City of Victoria. Speaker noted many programs locally such as the P.A.C.E program and

     programs available through organizations like the Y.M.C.A. Speaker expressed concern with the
     permanency of the agreement noting there is no opt-out feature.

     B. Armstrong, Rodney Rd — re: item 4.1 — Speaker noted that the CRD Arts and Culture program
     is a CRD initiative and not a City of Victoria one. Speaker expressed support for regional arts and
     culture noting many residents of Langford travel around the CRD. Speaker noted that currently
     there is a need to travel outside of the City to experience arts and culture. Speaker also noted
     interest in seeing a report regarding the program in the future.

     S. Rossander, Ravensview Dr — re: item 4.1— Speaker expressed support for a report being
     written exploring the pros and cons of joining the CRD Arts and Culture program. Speaker
     expressed opposition to joining the CRD Arts and Culture program noting the permanency of the
     agreement as there is no opt-out feature.

     L. Foxall, Players Dr — re: item 9.4 -- Speaker noted the minutes did not mention the
     repercussions of the social media clause, only the policies. re: item 4.1 — Speaker noted that they
     have received feedback from residents wishing not to partner with the City of Victoria. Speaker
     noted that the City partners with many neighbouring municipalities who share borders on
     numerous issues and in order to keep investment and jobs in the City, Langford should not
     partner with the CRD on this program. Speaker expressed concern with the permanency of the
     agreement as there is no opt-out feature. Speaker noted an arts and culture center could be
     built at the new university in partnership with nearby municipalities.

     S. Sifert. Walfred Rd - re: 4.1 - Concerned about the cost of 2023 permits vs. 2021/2022.12.4% is

     Homeless Society's new property.

     T. Wright, Commander Crt - re: item 9.2 - Expressed opposition to the tax increase. Will have an

     J.C., Claude Rd - re: Ridgeview PI - Expressed a need for more help. Speaker expressed not
     enough is being done to assist residents.

     M. Wignall, Selwyn Rd - re: item 6.2 - Expressed concern that their views at public participation
     were not captured accurately. re: item 9.2- Expressed concern about the numbers of the tax
     increase. Expressed concern regarding line item on page 3 of the budget.

     M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance responded and clarified the percentages.

     A. Rossander, Ravensview Dr - re: item 9.3 - Expressed concern regarding the tax increase.
     Speaker asked if the Mayor be happy with the increase if they were a resident of Langford.
     Expressed concern that the current Mayor has not enlisted the assistance of the former Mayor.

     S. Sifert, Walfred Rd - re: item 9.3 - Expressed gratitude to the mayor for allowing residents of
     RidgeView Apartments to speak. Expressed opposition to the proposed budget. Expressed
     concern regarding the increase of expenditures to the consults. Expressed concern regarding the
     increase to the training and travel allowance. Expressed concern regarding the increase to
     adverting for planning and parks departments. Expressed concern regarding the increase to
     community events expenditures. Expressed concern regarding the increase to tourism
     expenditures. Expressed total increase is $390,453 or over 64% from the previous year.

Expressed concern why are more consultants are hired. Expressed concern why can't there be
better rates. Expressed concern why do staff travel so much. Expressed concern why is the City
buying the YMCA.

S. Rossander, Ravensview Dr - re: item 10.3 - Speaker asked why this bylaw is necessary.

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance responded that there is standard wording in the bylaw. The
City has no plans to borrow the funds, but the City is required to have it as part of the banking
agreements.

M.L. Taylor, Claude Rd - re: RidgeView Apartments - Expressed great concern regarding the
current situation with their home. Expressed concern regarding next steps.

C. Aubrey, Fire Chief responded that the resident reach out to them at the firehall, and they will
assist any way they can.

Nicholas Johal, Walfred PI - re: item 9.3 - Expressed disappointment that the budget didn't
prioritize the turf and light field. Speaker is discouraged by the lack of communication and
partnership with the local school district, and minor sports leagues teams regarding the
decision. The speaker inquired who was consulted regarding the decision. Expressed concern
regarding the tax increase and the financial impact to residents.

W. Hobbs, Luxton Rd - re: item 9.3 - Expressed support regarding the number of increases to
firefighters. Expressed support for the increase of RCMP police officers.

L. Foxall, Players Dr - re: item 9.3 - Expressed opposition to the increase and the five-year
financial plan. Expressed concern that Council did not work to decrease the budget. Expressed
suggestions to decrease the budget. Raise fees in the development community too offset taxes.
Raise the rate of amenity fees to pay for new RCMP building. Expressed concern that public
questions were not answered.

R. Taylor, Claude Rd - re: RidgeView Apartments - Expressed concern regarding not being
notified sooner about the situation in the building. Expressed concern regarding next steps.

S. Costello, Robalee PI - re: item 9.3 - Expressed that they are a 52-year resident of the City.
Expressed support for the budget. Expressed support for the financial director. Expressed that
the taxes should be higher, in order to have all of the available amenities.

S. Perry, Glen Lake Rd - re: item 9.2 and 9.3 - Expressed that an increase in City staff is not
necessary. Expressed that work loads have decreased. Speaker stated that Council and staff
need to work harder. Expressed concern that questions submitted have not been answered.

C. Wright, Commander Crt - re: item 9.3 - Expressed concern that the non-property tax revenues
are not being used to reduce property taxes.

W. Bowers, Millstream Rd - re: item 9.3 - Expressed concern that the public is being ignored.
Expressed concern why didn't the purchase of the YMCA go to referendum. Speaker stated that
if there is not enough funding for the RCMP building, that travel expenses should be cut.

V. Barrow, Happy Valley Rd - re: item 9.3 - Expressed concern about the increase of taxes.
Expressed concern about living on a pension and the future increases of expenses.

J. Patterson, Lodmell Rd - re: item 9.3 - Expressed opposition to the tax increase. Expressed
concern that the young families will lose housing.

C. Legacy, Artesian Crt - re: item 9.3 - Expressed support for the proposed budget. Speaker
stated instead of lending the YMCA money, the City should buy it.

M. Wignall, Selwyn Rd - re: item 9.3 - Speaker discussed the fees of the budget. Speaker
discussed the non-property revenues being used for property taxes. Speaker discussed training
and travel expenses. Expressed concern regarding some previous events not being funded again.
Expressed concern regarding the Latoria Rd. turf field.

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance responded that the events on page 23 are budgeted as a
group. Regarding revenues, it is the City's practice to budget conservatively. We look at past
year trends when looking at a budget.

L. Foxall, Players Dr- re: RidgeView apartments. Speaker inquired if there is an ambassador for
residents at Ridgeview. re: item 9.3 - Speaker stated to look to increasing development
community. Expressed concern regarding paying taxes in July.

W. Hobbs, Luxton Rd - re: item 9.3 - Speaker inquired about the following years tax rate.
Speaker stated that the budget is actually an increase of 6% from last year.

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance responded the rates were 2.95% last year, 2021 5.84%. Just
over 6% for last 3 years.

C. Lervold, Glen Lake Rd - re: item 9.3 - Expressed opposition to the proposed budget. Expressed
disappointment that their questions have not been answered. Expressed concern that
negotiations were compromised. Expressed concern that the YMCA has become a priority over
the RCMP building.

S. Sifert, Walfred Rd - re: item 9.3 - Expressed concern regarding the Council listening to the
community.

Mayor Goodmanson confirmed events are still running, just a separate line item on budget.

A. Rossander, Ravensview Dr - re: item 9.3 - Speaker wanted clarification of line items of the
budget. Speaker believes the calculation to be misleading.

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance responded that the numbers are correct. In 2024, 50 million
compared to 45 million in 2023. Not depicting that as a total.

motions.source_motion_text:
THAT Council:

                   1.   Proceed with consideration of First Reading of Bylaw No. 2154 to amend
                        the text of the CD3 zone to allow for a group daycare with 53 children at
                        1331 Westhills Drive subject to the following terms and conditions:

                        a.   That the applicant, prior to Bylaw Adoption, registers a Section 219
                             covenant in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees to the
                             following:

                             i.    That the following Transit Demand Management strategies be
                                   implemented and maintained for all office users, in accordance
                                   with the Parking Study completed by Watt Consulting Group,
                                   dated December 15t, 2023

                                   1. Guaranteed Ride Home program with a minimum of 8
                                      reimbursable trips per employee per year; and

                                   2. Commuter financial incentives, providing employees with at
                                      least $1.55 per day cash out for not using a single occupant
                                      vehicle as their travel mode.

                             ii.   That no parking stalls be assigned to specific users with the
                                   exception of the daycare leaseholder and that all parking be
                                   provided on a first-come-first-served basis, with the exception
                                   of accessible parking stalls and designated pick-up and drop-off
                                   stalls for the daycare use.

             AND

             2. Direct staff to provide notice that Council will consider issuing a Development
             Variance Permit for the property at 1331 Westhills Drive with the following
             variance to Zoning Bylaw No. 300:

                        a.   That Section 4.01.01 be varied to reduce the required parking from
                             126 to 118 parking stalls.

5.   PUBLIC HEARINGS

     5.1   BYLAW NO. 1927

           "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 706, (957 Walfred Road), Bylaw No. 1927,
           2023".

           The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1927 at 7:05 pm.

           Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised Kyle Velikovsky has applied on behalf of
           White Wolf Homes Ltd. to amend the zoning of 957 Walfred Road from the RS1
           (Residential Small Lot 1) Zone to RT1 (Residential Townhouse 1) Zone.

           This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of approximately 17
           townhome units.

           In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

               a.   That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density, the following
                    contributions per dwelling unit:

                    i. $610 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; and
                    ii. $3,660 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;

               b. That the applicant, prior to Bylaw Adoption, discharge the previous rezoning
                  covenant and register a new Section 219 covenant in priority of all other charges
                  on title, that agrees to the following:
                  i. That the following will be provided and implemented to Bylaw No. 1000
                  standards to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to the issuance
                  of a building permit:

                        1. Full frontage improvements, inclusive of constructing a cul de sac and
                        bowtie parking, connecting the existing sidewalk on Hinks Road to the on-
                        site pathway, boulevard, and streetlighting. It must also include
                        improvements to the frontage of 955 Walfred Road;
                        2. A storm water management plan; and
                        3. A construction parking management plan.

                    ii. That a separate covenant be registered prior to the registration of a strata
                    plan for the proposed development agreeing that the garages are to be used for
                    the parking of vehicles and not the storage of items preventing the parking of
                    vehicles therein, in favour of the strata.

                    iii. That tree protection measures, inclusive of tree protection fencing, are
                    implemented prior to commencement of work to protect the trees identified for
                    retention in the arborist report throughout the construction period;
                    iv. That all concrete used on-site will utilize ready-mix concrete that meets or
                    exceeds the weighted average Global Warming Potential targets based on
                    Concrete BC Baseline (average) mix data, and that prior to the issuance of a
                    Building Permit the applicant shall provide a Type III Environmental Product

                      Declaration that is 3rd party verified specifying the total Global Warming
                      Potential value and confirming that the proposed development meets the
                      requirements of Low Carbon Concrete Policy POL-0167-PLAN;
                      v. That a Statutory Right of Way be registered over the public pathway prior to
                      the issuance of a building permit;
                      vi. That the public pathway shall be demonstrated within the landscape plan
                      and be clearly delineated to the satisfaction of the Director of Parks, Recreation,
                      and Facilities.

              In addition, Council has resolved to amend the text of Schedule AD of the Zoning Bylaw
              No. 300 to remove the amenity contributions related to Bylaw No. 1261;

              Council has also, by resolution, authorized the Director of Planning to issue the following
              variances within the form and character development permit:

                      a. Section 6.28.07(1)(a) to reduce the front lot line setback from 3 m to 1.2m;
                      and
                      b. Section 6.28.07(1)(d) to reduce the rear lot line setback from 5.5 m to 1.5 m

              Subject to the condition that the variances are only granted for the development of the
              townhouse project as shown at Public Hearing

              This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan Neighbourhood
              designation.

             Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local Government
             Act.

             Mayor Goodmanson called a first time for presentations.

             Kyle Velikovsky on behalf of White Wolf Homes Ltd, provided an overview of the
             proposed development to Council.

             Mayor Goodmanson called a second time for presentations.

             T. Parkinson, Walfred Rd - The speaker expressed concern regarding blasting, parking
             and water management in the proposed development. The speaker expressed concern
             regarding their loss of privacy. The speaker expressed concern regarding the changes the
             development will bring to their family's lives.

             Mayor Goodmanson called a third time for presentations.

             N. Johal, Walfred PI - The speaker expressed support for the development.

             Mayor Goodmanson called for a final time for presentations.

             None presented.

             Mayor Goodmanson declared the Public Hearing for Bylaw No.1927 closed at 7:26 pm.

        Declaration that is 3rd party verified specifying the total Global
        Warming Potential value and confirming that the proposed
        development meets the requirements of Low Carbon Concrete
        Policy POL-0167-PLAN;

    vii. That electric heat pumps be required as a condition of zoning.

southern interior side lot line, reducing the requirement from 1.2 m to 1
m along the park boundary.

6.   PUBLIC HEARINGS

     6.1   BYLAW NO. 2082

           "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 679, (Omnibus No. 60 — Various Housekeeping
           Items), Bylaw No. 2082, 2023".

           The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2082 at 7:52 pm.

           Director of Planning & Subdivision, Matthew Baldwin advised The City of Langford is
           proposing to amend Zoning Bylaw No. 300 in the following ways:

           • By introducing "accessory dormitories which may include a kitchenette" as a
           permitted use in the CD2 (Hull's Field) zone;

           • By removing restrictions on where apartments may occur in the City Centre
           Pedestrian (CCP) Zone excluding Peatt Road, Claude Road, Bryn Maur Avenue, Jacklin
           Road and Veterans Memorial Parkway;

           • By consolidating all daycare capacity exemptions from each zone into Part 3 of the
           Zoning bylaw.

           • By allowing two-family dwellings within the R2 (One-and Two-family Residential)
           zones on lots less than 600m2 but not less than 500m2 if the lot width is 17m.

           • By introducing requirements for accessible parking in all types of multi-family
           residential development.

           Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local Government
           Act.

           Mayor Goodmanson called a first time for presentations.

             M. Wignall, Selwyn Road - Speaker inquired if the changes to the R2 zone are
             independent of new housing legislation.

             M. Baldwin, Director of Planning and Subdivision responded - amendment is
             independent of the new Provincial legislation.

             Mayor Goodmanson called a second time for presentations.

             None presented.

             Mayor Goodmanson called a third time for presentations.

             None presented.

             Mayor Goodmanson declared the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2082 closed at 7:56 pm.
